page: Google Cloud Platform e2-micro is a shared-core virtual machine instance within the e2 family. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.2 GHz. The instance is configured with 2 vCPUs allocated from a 1/8 shared physical core, 1 physical core total, and 2 threads per core. It includes 1.0 GB of system memory, yielding 0.5 GB of RAM per core. There is no bundled local storage or GPU hardware, and it does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluations place the performance of this instance in the bottom 10% across all categories. The stress-ng single-core CPU performance score is 132.9, and the multi-core score is 171.0. Memory bandwidth is limited, with cached small-block read speeds at 9.73 GB/sec, uncached large-block reads at 0.1 GB/sec, and uncached large-block writes at 1.33 GB/sec. Passmark CPU and memory scores are 201.56 and 176.45 respectively. Database operations under Passmark score 57.19, Redis SET operations reach 0.2 million operations per second, and static web serving throughput is measured at 0.17 GB/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, this instance represents a low-resource tier designed for minimal resource consumption. The shared-core CPU allocation and low memory capacity introduce significant performance tradeoffs, making it unsuitable for CPU-intensive or memory-heavy applications. It is best utilized for lightweight, non-critical workloads such as basic microservices, simple development or testing environments, low-traffic static web serving, and small-scale utility scripts.
